the ion outflow from Mars is dominated by oxygen ions and is similar to the ion outflow above the Earth's polar cap, with a mass flux of ∼3x1025 ions s−1, and is comparable in magnitude to the ionospheric loss rate of Venus.
Mars loses oxygen to space at a rate of 3 x 1026 ions s-1, and this is due to ionospheric outflows and pick-up by the solar wind.

Mars has an ionospheric out-flow of oxygen ions that is comparable to that of the Earth and that the planet loses its present total oxygen content (contained mostly in the atmosphere) in less than a hundred million years.
